recent_trades.summary: Adding to ISRG on strong upside thesis and positive coverage ahead of July 16 earnings.
recent_trades.reasoning: ISRG shows resilience with +0.19% today versus broader market declines; recent coverage highlights 35% upside from robotic surgery growth and procedure recovery. Reallocation from NVDA increases this position modestly while staying under 20% single-name cap; fits defensive growth tilt as energy theme is already well represented.

recent_trades.summary: Trimming NVDA to reduce chip exposure amid continued AI selloff and reallocate to healthcare.
recent_trades.reasoning: NVDA has been weak intraday and aligns with the sector selloff triggered by SK Hynix weakness; proceeds fund addition to a higher-conviction name while respecting the 20% gross exposure and single-name limits. Sizing keeps NVDA below 2% to limit drag if weakness persists.

recent_trades.summary: Initiate a modest EOG position as renewed Hormuz disruption headlines continue to favor high-quality upstream oil producers.
recent_trades.reasoning: EOG offers additional upstream crude exposure without overconcentrating further in integrated majors. The current tape shows energy among the better-performing groups intraday, EOG sentiment is notably positive, and the Reuters/Yahoo headline flow continues to reinforce a concrete supply-risk backdrop tied to the Strait of Hormuz. A 4% starter size respects that this is still an event-driven trade and that we already own CVX and COP, but broadens our energy exposure into a high-quality E&P name that can benefit more directly from sustained higher crude prices.

recent_trades.summary: Trim RTX to reduce concentration after the sharp defense-driven run while keeping a meaningful position.
recent_trades.reasoning: RTX remains fundamentally supported by the same defense-spending and missile-production theme, but at nearly 16% of portfolio value it has become one of the portfolio's largest single-name exposures after today's add and subsequent strength. With no materially new defense catalyst since the last buy, trimming back to 12% improves diversification and preserves gains without abandoning the thesis. Sizing stays substantial because the macro backdrop still favors defense names.

recent_trades.summary: Open a 4.5% long position in SLB after it won a major Eni offshore contract, a clear catalyst.
recent_trades.reasoning: SLB's OneSubsea division secured a major umbilical contract from Eni for the Baleine Phase 3 project. This is a concrete positive development that, combined with elevated oil prices from the Strait of Hormuz crisis, supports the stock. Position size is kept moderate to stay under the 100% long limit.

recent_trades.summary: Exit Oracle entirely to rotate capital into SLB, which just won a major contract.
recent_trades.reasoning: ORCL has been a weak performer and offers no near-term catalyst. Selling frees up capacity to add SLB, an energy services name with specific positive news and oil-market tailwinds.

recent_trades.summary: Adding to ISRG ahead of July 16 earnings where analyst consensus sees +35% upside, with robotic surgery adoption accelerating and the position currently small at 4.7%.
recent_trades.reasoning: ISRG reports earnings July 16 — in 3 days. A Yahoo/SA analyst note today specifically highlights '+35% upside, compelling buy before July 16.' The robotic surgery adoption curve remains intact, and ISRG has held up relatively well (-2.39% from my entry) despite broad market weakness. Increasing from ~4.7% to ~8% weight makes sense given the imminent catalyst. The Iran tensions don't directly impair surgical robotics demand. I'm funding this from the ORCL proceeds.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting ORCL as the stock continues to drift near 30-day lows with no specific Oracle catalyst visible and -4.26% unrealized loss, freeing capital for higher-conviction opportunities.
recent_trades.reasoning: ORCL is my weakest holding at -4.26% unrealized loss. It sits near its 30-day low ($133.85) with no Oracle-specific positive catalyst in today's news. The position has been a drag and the general chip/tech weakness from SK Hynix and the Iran risk-off environment add headwinds. My last action on ORCL was a SELL on 7/10 — this position was re-entered before that (my avg cost is $140.29 vs current $134.30), and I'm now trimming to zero to redeploy. The original thesis of cloud/AI tailwinds has not materialized into price action and there's no specific upcoming catalyst that would change this near-term. Freeing up ~3.8% of portfolio value allows me to add to higher-conviction positions like ISRG before its July 16 earnings.

recent_trades.summary: Initiating 4% EOG position to gain from oil price surge on US-Iran tensions.
recent_trades.reasoning: EOG has strong +0.58 sentiment and benefits directly as a producer from higher crude prices; fits the portfolio's increased energy tilt (already in XOM, CVX, SLB) without exceeding position limits. Sizing to 4% keeps it below single-name cap and maintains diversification.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting remaining AVGO to reduce chip exposure amid ongoing semiconductor selloff.
recent_trades.reasoning: AVGO has lagged amid the chip sector weakness triggered by SK Hynix; proceeds will fund higher-conviction energy exposure. Current weight ~3% is trimmed fully as part of broader de-risking of AI-chip names.

recent_trades.summary: Initiating AXP position on JPMorgan upgrade noting affluent customer base is shielded from Iran conflict fallout.
recent_trades.reasoning: AXP has been upgraded by Wall Street analysts today, with JPMorgan specifically noting its affluent customer base is 'relatively shielded' from Iran war fallout. This defensive quality within financials is attractive in the current geopolitical environment. The stock is near its 30-day midpoint with neutral price action, suggesting the upgrade hasn't been fully priced in. Sentiment is solidly positive at +0.25.

recent_trades.summary: Increase RTX as defense spending momentum and missile-production expansion remain one of the clearest specific catalysts in the portfolio.
recent_trades.reasoning: RTX continues to show supportive intraday resilience and positive news flow tied to defense demand. The specific driver remains the reported Trump trillion-dollar defense push and the previously cited missile-production expansion backdrop, both of which directly support RTX’s defense systems and sustainment businesses. The position is already working, but at 14% it is still below the single-name cap and merits a modest increase because defense is one of the cleaner beneficiaries of the current geopolitical regime without requiring higher oil prices to hold gains.

recent_trades.summary: Trim Philip Morris because it is lagging despite the risk-off tape and offers less immediate catalyst support than our energy and defense holdings.
recent_trades.reasoning: PM has positive news sentiment but the stock is essentially flat versus our cost and down on the day, suggesting limited near-term momentum. In the current environment, capital is better concentrated in names with a clearer direct catalyst from geopolitics, especially energy and defense, rather than a defensive staple with no fresh company-specific driver. This is a trim, not an exit, because PM still offers defensive characteristics and income support.

recent_trades.summary: Add modestly to ConocoPhillips as live Hormuz disruption headlines continue to support upstream oil exposure.
recent_trades.reasoning: COP remains a smaller energy position than CVX despite the same macro tailwind, and upstream producers typically benefit more directly from sustained crude risk premium. The Reuters/Yahoo flow today keeps confirming renewed Strait of Hormuz closure and cargo-charge escalation, while COP is holding near its 30-day high with positive 5-day and 30-day trends. Sizing remains moderate because this is still headline-driven and we already hold substantial energy exposure through CVX.

recent_trades.summary: Adding to XOM as Trump formally reinstates Iran blockade with 20% Strait of Hormuz cargo tariff — a policy escalation beyond today's earlier military posturing.
recent_trades.reasoning: The specific driver: Reuters confirms Trump has reinstated the Iran blockade AND imposed a 20% tariff on Strait of Hormuz cargo. This is a formal policy action, materially more concrete than the closure threat I traded on this morning. XOM is at $144.13 near its 30-day high, confirming price momentum. Current weight is 4.46%; bringing to 7% adds meaningful energy exposure within the constraint. The formal blockade/tariff creates a sustained oil supply premium, not a one-day spike.

recent_trades.summary: Adding to SLB on fresh Eni offshore contract wins and sustained oil-price momentum.
recent_trades.reasoning: SLB just announced major EPC and umbilical contracts for Eni's Baleine Phase 3 and other offshore growth; combined with the geopolitical oil rally and positive sentiment, this justifies increasing the position using HON sale proceeds. Sizing keeps single-name exposure well below 20% cap and aligns with energy theme without adding net exposure.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting full HON position to rotate proceeds into energy on geopolitical tailwinds.
recent_trades.reasoning: HON has underperformed (-2.61% unrealized) amid industrial-sector volatility; selling frees capital to concentrate in SLB which benefits directly from both the oil surge and specific new offshore contracts. This reduces cyclical industrial exposure while staying within all risk limits.

recent_trades.summary: Initiating 4% XOM position to gain direct exposure to surging oil prices driven by US-Iran escalation.
recent_trades.reasoning: XOM benefits as a large integrated major with upstream leverage, strong balance sheet, and dividend support; sized at 4% as part of energy rotation while keeping all positions under 20% and total gross exposure limits.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting LIN to realize 5.5% gain and rotate proceeds into energy amid oil surge from Iran tensions.
recent_trades.reasoning: LIN has performed well but offers less direct upside than energy in the current geopolitical regime; selling frees capital for reallocation while respecting single-name and gross exposure limits.

recent_trades.summary: Adding to RTX as Iran Strait of Hormuz escalation and Trump's trillion-dollar defense push provide dual catalysts for defense aerospace names.
recent_trades.reasoning: RTX is currently at 12.61% weight, up 7.85% from my entry — thesis is strongly intact. Today brings two converging catalysts: (1) Iran reinstating the Strait of Hormuz blockade + US-Iran escalation directly benefits defense contractors as military readiness spending increases; (2) 'Trump's Trillion-Dollar Defense Push Could Be a Boon for Lockheed, RTX, Boeing and Northrop' — RTX explicitly named. The Houthis striking Saudi Arabia and UK banning Iranian groups escalates the regional conflict. RTX is one of the primary beneficiaries. Adding from 12.6% toward 15% captures this renewed catalyst while staying within the 20% single-name limit.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting residual AMD position as AI chip selloff directly names AMD as a laggard alongside broader semiconductor weakness.
recent_trades.reasoning: AMD is a tiny 1.96% position that I've already been reducing. Today's news explicitly names 'Nvidia, Broadcom, AMD Lead AI Chip Stock Selloff After SK Hynix Slump' — AMD is one of the three names called out. The negative sentiment score (-0.09) confirms this. The position is essentially flat (-0.03%) from entry, giving me a clean exit. Holding a sub-2% position in a sector that is selling off with negative news flow is not worth the risk. Exiting frees up cash and reduces chip concentration.

recent_trades.summary: Trimming AVGO as AI chip selloff led by SK Hynix slump and Iran risk-off creates new near-term headwinds for semiconductor names.
recent_trades.reasoning: My last buy of AVGO on 2026-07-10 was predicated on the Apple $30B AI chip deal as a positive catalyst. Today, a new negative catalyst has emerged: 'Nvidia, Broadcom, AMD Lead AI Chip Stock Selloff After SK Hynix Slump' — this is a sector-wide derating event affecting AVGO directly. Additionally, the Iran blockade reinstated creates broad risk-off sentiment that hits high-beta tech harder. The stock is only up ~1.5% from my entry, giving me room to trim before the selloff deepens. Reducing from ~9.7% to ~7% weight frees up cash for potential redeployment and reduces chip sector concentration.

recent_trades.summary: Trim AMD as chip stocks weaken on fresh sector-wide AI semiconductor pressure while geopolitical risk favors reducing cyclical tech beta.
recent_trades.reasoning: AMD remains profitable and the longer-term AI thesis is still intact, so I am not exiting outright. However, fresh intraday news explicitly says Nvidia, Broadcom, and AMD are leading an AI chip selloff after the SK Hynix slump, while the broader market is also risk-off on Iran/Hormuz headlines. That combination raises near-term downside volatility in semis more than in the rest of the book. Trimming from 7.48% to 5% reduces exposure to the weakest tape segment while retaining participation if the selloff stabilizes.

recent_trades.summary: Increase ConocoPhillips to 16% weight as the Strait of Hormuz closure directly boosts oil prices and producer earnings.
recent_trades.reasoning: Multiple independent considerations converge: (1) Iran’s declared closure disrupts a critical oil transit route, (2) oil prices have jumped, (3) COP is a pure-play producer with leverage to spot prices, (4) defense‑energy rotation theme persists. The main risk is a rapid ceasefire, but the current news flow suggests escalation.

recent_trades.summary: Exit Dominion Energy entirely to rotate into a more direct crisis beneficiary.
recent_trades.reasoning: Dominion lacks a direct catalyst in the current Iran crisis, whereas oil producers stand to benefit from the Strait of Hormuz closure. Reallocating to ConocoPhillips offers better risk-adjusted return potential amid the supply shock.

recent_trades.summary: Tiny trim of Oracle to help bring total long exposure below 100%.
recent_trades.reasoning: Combined with the RTX trim, reducing ORCL by ~0.05% of portfolio value brings total long exposure from 100.05% to exactly 100.00%, satisfying the constraint.

recent_trades.summary: Trim RTX to exactly 20% weight to comply with the single-name exposure limit.
recent_trades.reasoning: After recent buying, the position drifted slightly above 20% due to price movement. A tiny trim ensures compliance with the hard 20% cap.

recent_trades.summary: Double our short on AMD to 10% as chip stocks sell off on SK Hynix slump and stretched AI valuations.
recent_trades.reasoning: AMD and the semiconductor sector are breaking down on negative earnings news from SK Hynix, and the broader risk-off environment accelerates the correction in high-beta tech names. We add to our existing profitable short to capitalize on further downside.

recent_trades.summary: Raise gold allocation to 10% as a safe haven amid escalating geopolitical risks and market turmoil.
recent_trades.reasoning: Gold historically outperforms during geopolitical crises and periods of uncertainty. The simultaneous U.S.-Iran escalation, oil shock, and negative market sentiment create a textbook environment for gold demand. We increase from 7.5% to 10%.

recent_trades.summary: Boost ConocoPhillips to 11% to capitalize on the oil supply shock from the Strait of Hormuz closure.
recent_trades.reasoning: Iran's closure of the Strait directly threatens global oil supply, a powerful catalyst for U.S. producers like COP. With tensions unlikely to ease quickly, oil prices should remain elevated, benefiting COP's earnings and share price.

recent_trades.summary: Increase RTX to the maximum 20% weight as renewed military conflict with Iran drives defense spending.
recent_trades.reasoning: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Trump's call for U.S. control, and Houthi retaliation threats create a sustained demand surge for defense contractors. RTX is a prime beneficiary with its missile systems and electronics. We increase from 15% to the maximum allowed weight given the high conviction.

recent_trades.summary: Sell General Electric entirely to pivot into pure defense and energy exposure.
recent_trades.reasoning: GE has aerospace exposure but the Iran conflict benefits pure defense names like RTX more directly, and rising oil prices could pressure commercial aerospace. The recent negative sentiment and already-down position make an exit timely.

recent_trades.summary: Trim Dominion Energy from 6.1% to 5% to fund higher-conviction positions.
recent_trades.reasoning: Utilities are defensive but lack the direct upside potential of energy and defense in the current geopolitical crisis. A modest trim provides capital for those trades while maintaining some utility exposure.

recent_trades.summary: Trim Philip Morris from 11.7% to 10% to reallocate into more direct crisis beneficiaries.
recent_trades.reasoning: While PM is defensive, the specific catalyst of Strait of Hormuz closure and U.S.-Iran escalation favors assets with direct upside (RTX, COP, GLD) over consumer staples. Reducing PM from an overweight funds these trades.

recent_trades.summary: Exit remaining Visa position to free capital for higher-conviction trades.
recent_trades.reasoning: Visa was trimmed on 7/6; with limited upside catalysts in the current risk-off environment, we close the position entirely to redeploy into crisis-linked assets.

recent_trades.summary: Short AMD as semiconductor selloff intensifies on Iran-driven risk-off.
recent_trades.reasoning: Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz is triggering a broad market selloff, with high-beta tech and semiconductor stocks leading losses. AMD is specifically cited among AI chip names slumping after SK Hynix's decline. We expect further downside as risk appetite evaporates. A 5% gross short position fits within our 20% short limit and adds a defensive hedge without overconcentrating.

recent_trades.summary: Initiating a 5% position in Intuitive Surgical ahead of an anticipated near-term catalyst on July 16.
recent_trades.reasoning: Street commentary points to a compelling fundamental setup and +35% upside ahead of a specific July 16 date, providing a strong idiosyncratic setup in a difficult macro tape.

recent_trades.summary: Initiating a 5% position in American Express as it receives analyst upgrades citing its affluent customer base as a defensive shield against the Iran conflict fallout.
recent_trades.reasoning: JPMorgan's latest upgrade specifically notes AXP can ride out the Iran war better than rivals due to its affluent customer base, providing defensive financial exposure in a risk-off tape.

recent_trades.summary: Adding to SLB on major new Eni offshore contracts and rising oil prices from geopolitical tensions.
recent_trades.reasoning: Positive contract catalysts, sector tailwinds from higher oil, and improved sentiment align to support a larger energy-services position; fits rotation away from weakening tech.

recent_trades.summary: Trimming AVGO to reduce AI-chip exposure amid ongoing selloff triggered by SK Hynix weakness.
recent_trades.reasoning: Negative sentiment and sector-specific pressure on chip stocks outweigh the earlier AI momentum that drove the July 10 entry; proceeds will support reallocation to energy.

recent_trades.summary: Boost gold allocation to 7.5% as a safe haven amid escalating Middle East conflict and broader market uncertainty.
recent_trades.reasoning: Gold traditionally surges during geopolitical crises when the risk of wider war and inflation rises. The failed Iran talks and Strait closure revive safe-haven demand that we had previously bet against on 7/10.

recent_trades.summary: Raise RTX to 15% weight as renewed military conflict with Iran spurs defense spending and primes contractor stocks.
recent_trades.reasoning: The collapse of diplomacy and new US military engagement signal a period of elevated defense expenditure. RTX, as a prime contractor, stands to see order flow increase. This reverses our 7/10 trim made when peace talks appeared to progress.

recent_trades.summary: Increase ConocoPhillips to 8% weight to benefit from the oil supply shock triggered by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
recent_trades.reasoning: The Hormuz closure directly threatens roughly 20% of global oil transit. COP, with its US onshore focus and minimal direct Hormuz exposure, should benefit from higher crude prices. This reverses our 7/10 trim that was based on easing tensions.

recent_trades.summary: Exit Mastercard entirely to raise capital for higher-conviction trades in defense, energy, and gold.
recent_trades.reasoning: MA faces negative sentiment following reports of a potential Vocalink majority sale, and the financials sector may not benefit from current geopolitical turmoil. Rotating out allows redeployment into names with direct crisis catalysts.

recent_trades.summary: Adding to WMT for its defensive qualities and recent positive news on Sam's Club wellness expansion.
recent_trades.reasoning: WMT shows +0.38 sentiment with news of wellness perks expansion and is a stable consumer staple that should hold up well in risk-off geopolitically driven markets; increases its weight modestly while funding the BAC trim.

recent_trades.summary: Further trimming BAC to lower financial exposure amid rising geopolitical and earnings volatility.
recent_trades.reasoning: BAC carries negative sentiment with fresh headlines on inflation risks, Fed volatility, worsening geopolitics, and banks kicking off Q2 earnings; this continues the earlier trim to reduce cyclical risk while macro uncertainties persist. Offsets the WMT add to keep cash near zero.

recent_trades.summary: Initiating a short position in AMD as a hedge against semiconductor downside driven by the Strait of Hormuz disruption.
recent_trades.reasoning: AMD is highly vulnerable to both the broader risk-off environment caused by an energy-driven inflation shock and the specific disruption to Asian tech manufacturing and shipping routes indicated by the plunge in the Kospi.

recent_trades.summary: Exiting NVDA completely due to the severe macro shock to semiconductor supply chains from the Strait of Hormuz closure.
recent_trades.reasoning: A major geopolitical supply shock typically triggers risk-off flows out of high-valuation tech, and the reported 9% drop in the Kospi confirms severe stress in Asian tech hardware markets. Continuing to hold a high-beta AI proxy through a massive global logistics and energy disruption is untenable.

recent_trades.summary: Initiate a 5% position in Disney as analyst upgrades and improving streaming fundamentals signal a potential re-rating.
recent_trades.reasoning: Disney's streaming losses are narrowing, its IP flywheel is delivering strong box office and theme park results, and several Wall Street analysts have highlighted the stock as a top pick or rebound play today. The stock trades near $96, not far from recent lows, offering a favorable risk/reward entry.

recent_trades.summary: Adding back to XOM as Strait of Hormuz closure creates acute oil supply disruption supporting higher energy prices for integrated majors.
recent_trades.reasoning: I trimmed XOM on July 10 on Iran diplomatic talks. The Hormuz Strait closure is a material reversal of that thesis. XOM as an integrated major with global supply chain benefits from higher oil prices. At 4.09% weight currently, adding to ~8% makes sense. XOM also benefits from being a US-based producer less exposed to Hormuz supply chains than pure refiners. The positive sentiment (+0.28) and energy sector tailwind from the geopolitical escalation support the position.
